rows.what_the_ink_shows: The upper interlinear insertion reads $N_{L/K}$ induit un isom: the first subscript is an L with a horizontal foot, followed by a slash and K (crops/15_scan144_L175_corollary_insert.jpg). The proof sentence again reads $N_{L/K}$ induit un isom, with the same clear L before the slash (crops/15_scan144_L175_proof_phrase.jpg). The displayed quotient likewise has $V_L/N_{L/K}(V_{L_0})$ (crops/15_scan144_L175_quotient.jpg). By contrast, the immediately preceding proof writes $N_{K/L}(\lambda)=\lambda^r$ and $\operatorname{Ker}(N_{K/L})$; the K before the slash and L after it are visible (crops/15_scan144_L175_correct_order_context.jpg). The corollary product and left-hand quotient also write $\operatorname{Ker}(N_{K/L})$. Thus the subscript reversal is present in the manuscript, not introduced by this transcription. Main-reader localization: the quoted applique occurrence is on scan 142 (crops/15_scan142_L175_norm_direction.jpg).
